name: DUCTLESS FUME HOOD
desc: Automatic Ductless Fume Hood engineered for advanced operator protection and hazardous vapor containment without requiring external ducting lines. Driven by an intelligent 7-inch color touchscreen controller with a high-efficiency multi-stage filtration system conforming to ASTM standards.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Ductless Fume Hood is an advanced recirculating containment system engineered to protect laboratory personnel from hazardous chemical vapors, fumes, and particulate matter without external ducting. Its operational principle integrates a high-efficiency multi-stage filtration train—comprising heavy-retention pre-filters, activated carbon, ammonia, formaldehyde, and HEPA modules—that adsorbs and neutralizes toxic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as xylene, toluene, acetone, methanol, and chloroform, as well as corrosive acid mists from hydrochloric, nitric, and sulfuric acids. A precisely controlled axial fan maintains a uniform face velocity of 0.4–0.6 m/s, ensuring inward airflow at the sash opening to prevent contaminant escape, while the 7-inch touchscreen PID controller continuously monitors chamber temperature, humidity, and filter saturation. This design conforms to ASHRAE 110:1995 and ASTM standards, making it suitable for histopathology staining, tissue processing, pharmaceutical quality control, chemical synthesis, and academic research where doctors, B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and chemists routinely handle formaldehyde, ammonia, and biological specimens.
sop: Ensure the ductless fume hood is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz single-phase supply and the main power switch is ON; verify the transparent acrylic sash is at the recommended working height.
Press the 'SET' button once on the PID controller to enter setpoint mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter, such as face velocity 0.5 m/s or chamber temperature 22 °C.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value and allow the controller to regulate fan speed automatically.
Allow the hood to run for at least 5 minutes before introducing chemicals; check the touchscreen for airflow, temperature, humidity, and filter saturation alarms.
Place chemical containers or apparatus at least 150 mm inside the hood, never blocking rear baffles or airflow slots.
Work with the sash at the designated safe opening height; avoid rapid arm movements that disrupt laminar containment.
After use, keep the hood running for 10–15 minutes to purge residual vapors before switching off.
Clean the interior epoxy resin work surface with a compatible neutral detergent; never use abrasive scrubbers or solvents that could damage the surface.

Safety Warning: Never use perchloric acid, highly reactive metals, or open flames inside the ductless hood; if the filter saturation alarm sounds or a strong odor is detected, immediately stop work, close the sash, and contact qualified service personnel.
